title: Microrequest Queue + QA Gaps — Rapid Synthesis
body:
Purpose:
Quick, consumable synthesis of small-scope customer asks (microrequests) that are high friction in product onboarding or daily ops, plus a lightweight QA gap inventory to fast-track fixes into next two sprints. Intended for PM + Eng Triage. Not a full roadmap; these are surgical wins that reduce churn or unblock enterprise deals.

Context and approach:
- Source window: 2028-09-01 to 2028-11-03. Inputs: support threads, CSM call notes, bug reports from frontline engineers, partner onboarding checklists.
- Goal: surface 8–12 candidate microrequests with owner suggestions, estimated effort (L/M/H), and a short test-case or repro note for QA. Also call out recurring test coverage gaps (observability, happy-path, edge-case) that increase time-to-closure.
- Tone: informal; contains notes-to-self and unresolved questions for product review.

Representative customer quotes (verbatim snippets):
- "When a request times out our app retried and doubled cost — need clearer retry guidance + default backoff for hosted API." — fintech POC
- "Embedding similarity scores drifted after model upgrade; we had no way to pin or compare versions in console." — analytics startup
- "We keep losing custom role bindings after export/import of workspace config in private deployments." — regulated health customer

Microrequest candidates (ID, short desc, why it matters, repro/test pointer, effort, suggested owner):

MR-101: Hosted API default client-side retry snippet + recommended backoff
- Why: multiple customers reimplement inconsistent retry leading to duplicate charges and higher tail latency.
- Repro/test: simulate 500 gateway flaps in test harness; verify recommended snippet results in <=1 retry and exponential backoff.
- Effort: Low
- Owner: SDK/Developer-Experience (Liam)

MR-102: Console: model-version diff tool for embedding regressions
- Why: customers need quick A/B comparison when Redwood rolls models (or recommends variants). Prevents SRE escalations and trust loss.
- Repro/test: create two index snapshots, run sample queries, verify side-by-side score tables and change highlights.
- Effort: Medium
- Owner: Product-Hosted-API + Console (Sofia)

MR-103: Dedicated capacity alert: predict spike exhaustion window in Console
- Why: customers surprised by burst exhaustion during batch jobs; small UX fix could reduce support tickets.
- Repro/test: apply synthetic throughput spike in staging and confirm warning shown 10–15m before SLA breach.
- Effort: Medium
- Owner: Dedicated Product + Observability (Marcus)

MR-104: KB: how quantization affects token-level cost estimates (simple table)
- Why: confusion during pre-sale and onboarding; affects purchase decisions for Dedicated/Private.
- Repro/test: sanity check against known quantized model run in bench; publish table.
- Effort: Low
- Owner: Applied ML + Solutions Eng

MR-105: Private deployment: role-binding import/export fix (permissions persist)
- Why: enterprise stuck during cutover; security teams block without deterministic exports.
- Repro/test: export workspace config, re-import, confirm bindings identical; add regression test in infra-e2e.
- Effort: High (but high impact)
- Owner: Private Deployments (Noah)

MR-106: Small telemetry: attach model-variant id to all failed-response traces
- Why: debugging time reduced from days to hours when variant present.
- Repro/test: force variant mismatch errors in dev, ensure trace contains variant id.
- Effort: Low
- Owner: Observability (Marcus)

MR-107: Billing UI: preview incremental cost for enabling caching on route
- Why: customers hesitate to enable cache due to unclear cost tradeoffs. Small UI estimation would increase adoption of caching (cost-reduction feature).
- Repro/test: mock toggle in console and verify preview calculation matches backend sim.
- Effort: Medium
- Owner: Console + Billing (Sofia)

MR-108: SDK: streaming reconnect guidance + sample snippet across languages
- Why: customers building chat UI see partial streams on flaky networks; standardized guidance reduces client code complexity.
- Repro/test: simulate intermittent socket loss and verify client behavior follows sample guidance.
- Effort: Low
- Owner: Developer Experience (Liam)

QA gap inventory (themes + examples):
- Flaky e2e coverage around streaming recovery paths. Current CI has unit + integration but missing simulated network flakiness tests. Result: intermittent regressions slip to prod.
- Sparse coverage for model-migration telemetry: no automated tests that assert embed/score deltas post-migration.
- Permission import/export in private deployments lacks e2e fixture that exercises role edge-cases (nested groups, external IDs).
- Billing preview math not exercised in UI tests; several UI/backend calc mismatches were found manually.

Proposed QA quick fixes (cheap, high leverage):
- Add a lightweight chaos test for streaming: local proxy that drops packets/interrupts TCP on CI for 2–3 runs per day (Low effort)
- Add a nightly model-migration smoke test that runs a canonical prompt set on two variants and records drift metrics; fail if > threshold (Medium effort)
- Add import/export role roundtrip test to private-deployments e2e and mark as required for releases (Medium effort)
- Add a unit+integration test for billing preview math in console repo linked to backend calc (Low effort)

Open questions / tradeoffs to raise in PM sync:
- For MR-102 (model-version diff): scope — quick CSV export + simple diff vs. fully integrated console side-by-side UI. Tradeoff: shipping CSV helps customers now (low effort) but reduces Console uplift.
- MR-105 (role-binding): is there appetite to prioritize ahead of other high-effort infra work? This is blocking one enterprise deal with >$300k ARR potential.
- Telemetry variant tagging (MR-106): does this increase PII risk for sensitive deployments? Need security sign-off for including variant identifiers in traces for private deployments.

Suggested next steps (short list):
1) Triage session (30m) with DevEx, Console, Private Deployments, Observability — schedule this week (owner: Priya).
2) Immediately slot MR-101, MR-106, MR-108 into next sprint as they are low-effort and high-customer-call-frequency. (owner: respective leads)
3) Build quick CSV export prototype for MR-102 as a minimal first step; evaluate adoption before full UI work. (owner: Sofia)
4) For MR-105, prepare a commercial mitigation note for CSM to use while infra backlog is negotiated (owner: Noah).

Decision log / short history:
- This doc consolidates microrequests surfaced in three recent enterprise escalations and 42 support threads. Previously attempted mitigation for retry guidance lived in SDK snippets but was fragmented across languages.

Notes to self / friction points:
- We need a single canonical place for small-playbook fixes (microrequests) with quick PR turnaround. Drive docs are chaotic — consider a short lived Linear queue label: "microrequest-ship".
- Some customers will accept a docs-only mitigation; others require code/console changes. Track mitigation channel in ticket.

Appendix: quick contact matrix
- Developer Experience: Liam O'Connor (liam@redwood.ai)
- Console PM: Sofia Ruiz (sofia@redwood.ai)
- Observability: Marcus Chen (marcus@redwood.ai)
- Private Deployments: Noah Patel (noah@redwood.ai)

End of snapshot.
